extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of classical philosophy; people studying Plato's Republic and political/educational theory
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for selecting, educating, and characterizing the guardians/philosopher‑kings and for diagnosing forms of government, as set out in Plato's Republic (Books VII–VIII). Useful for anyone modeling ideal rulers, staged education, or political degeneration in fiction or theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectical skill as the supreme study
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialectic...is the coping-stone of the sciences, and is set over them; no other science can be placed higher—the nature of knowledge can no further go?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialectic is the highest educational aim: training in the art of asking and answering questions is the pinnacle of the curriculum and the chief test of true philosophical capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gifts for chosen rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: The same natures must still be chosen, and the preference again given to the surest and the bravest, and, if possible, to the fairest; and, having noble and generous tempers, they should also have the natural gifts which will facilitate their education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for inborn qualities that facilitate education: keenness, ready powers of acquisition, noble/generous temper — these natural gifts make a candidate suited to lengthy intellectual training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keenness and quick acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Such gifts as keenness and ready powers of acquisition; for the mind more often faints from the severity of study than from the severity of gymnastics: the toil is more entirely the mind’s own...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should demonstrate quick understanding and enthusiasm for learning; intellectual stamina is more decisive than bodily stamina for advanced study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good memory and love of labour
rubrics_metrics.description: Further, he of whom we are in search should have a good memory, and be an unwearied solid man who is a lover of labour in any line; or he will never be able to endure the great amount of bodily exercise and to go through all the intellectual discipline and study which we require of him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical requirement: sustained effort and reliable memory are necessary to complete the long, demanding educational pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wholehearted vocation (not half industrious and half idle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Her votary should not have a lame or halting industry—I mean, that he should not be half industrious and half idle: as, for example, when a man is a lover of gymnastic and hunting, and all other bodily exercises, but a hater rather than a lover of the labour of learning or listening or enquiring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid candidates with split priorities or divided vocations; true students of philosophy must be committed rather than partly attracted to mere physical/casual pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness and moral sensitivity to falsehood
rubrics_metrics.description: And as to truth...is not a soul equally to be deemed halt and lame which hates voluntary falsehood and is extremely indignant at herself and others when they tell lies, but is patient of involuntary falsehood...and has no shame at being detected?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing truth and being ashamed of ignorance/dishonesty are marks of moral character; tolerance of falsehood or complacency in ignorance are disqualifying traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession of cardinal virtues (temperance, courage, magnificence, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: And, again, in respect of temperance, courage, magnificence, and every other virtue, should we not carefully distinguish between the true son and the bastard?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess holistic virtue: multiple virtues must cohere; deficiency in any part weakens suitability for rulership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early foundation studies without compulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculation and geometry and all the other elements of instruction, which are a preparation for dialectic, should be presented to the mind in childhood; not, however, under any notion of forcing our system of education... Because a freeman ought not to be a slave in the acquisition of knowledge of any kind. Bodily exercise, when compulsory, does no harm to the body; but knowledge which is acquired under compulsion obtains no hold on the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce foundational subjects (math, geometry) in childhood but avoid coercion; make early learning playful to reveal natural bent and secure lasting knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical exposure and staged progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use compulsion, but let early education be a sort of amusement... The same practice may be followed, I said, in all these things—labours, lessons, dangers—and he who is most at home in all of them ought to be enrolled in a select number... After that time those who are selected from the class of twenty years old will be promoted to higher honour... those who have most of this comprehension... when they have arrived at the age of thirty have to be chosen... proved by the help of dialectic... Say five years, I replied; at the end of the time they must be sent down again into the den and compelled to hold any military or other office... And how long is this stage of their lives to last? Fifteen years, I answered; and when they have reached fifty years of age, then let those who still survive and have distinguished themselves... come at last to their consummation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a multi-stage training plan: childhood foundations, selective promotion around age 20, dialectic training and testing toward 30, field experience (~15 years), final elevation around 50; use staged practical tests (gymnastics, battle exposure, offices) to assess character and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution in introducing dialectic to avoid eristic lawlessness
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a danger lest they should taste the dear delight too early... youngsters... when they first get the taste in their mouths, argue for amusement, and are always contradicting and refuting others... And when they have made many conquests and received defeats... they violently and speedily get into a way of not believing anything which they believed before...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay deep dialectical training until maturity to prevent sophistic disputation (eristic) and moral instability; cultivate the pursuit of truth, not mere contradiction for amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steadfastness, orderliness and vocational exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: And did we not make special provision for this, when we said that the disciples of philosophy were to be orderly and steadfast, not, as now, any chance aspirant or intruder?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose candidates who demonstrate steady character and exclusive commitment to their educational/political vocation rather than opportunistic entrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to flattering influences of wealth and false parentage
rubrics_metrics.description: By way of parallel, imagine a suppositive son who is brought up in great wealth... when he learns that his alleged are not his real parents... he would diminish his honour and regard for them, and would become more devoted to the flatterers... Now all this is very natural in students of philosophy such as I have described... and also... most excusable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of social/root causes that may corrupt candidates (wealth, flatterers). Educational/proving stages must test moral stability against flattering influences and social disorientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal lifestyle and renunciation of private property for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: The governors, when appointed themselves, will take their soldiers and place them in houses such as we were describing, which are common to all, and contain nothing private, or individual; and about their property... they were to be warrior athletes and guardians, receiving from the other citizens, in lieu of annual payment, only their maintenance...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians should live communally with no private possessions and accept maintenance rather than private wealth to prevent corruption and conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal training for women insofar as nature permits
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not suppose that what I have been saying applies to men only and not to women as far as their natures can go.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include women in the same educational and civic roles when their natural capacities allow; apply selection and training fairly with regard to ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural priorities shape political character (music vs gymnastics)
rubrics_metrics.description: When your guardians are ignorant of the law of births... they will be unworthy to hold their fathers’ places, and when they come into power... they will soon be found to fail in taking care of us, the Muses, first by under-valuing music; which neglect will soon extend to gymnastic; and hence the young men of your State will be less cultivated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain cultural balance (music/culture and gymnastics) in education; neglecting music/culture breeds decline in cultivation and precipitates political degeneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character template for timocratic rulers (honour-based rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The spirit of contention and ambition... the timocratical man... more of self-assertion and be less cultivated, and yet a friend of culture; and he should be a good listener, but no speaker... rough with slaves... courteous to freemen... a lover of power and a lover of honour... a lover of gymnastic exercises and of the chase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying or selecting timocratic individuals: emphasize spirited ambition, military aptitude, pursuit of honor, roughness toward inferiors, and a mixed relation to culture and wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Features and defects of oligarchy (property-based rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A government resting on a valuation of property, in which the rich have power and the poor man is deprived of it... the inevitable division: such a State is not one, but two States, the one of poor, the other of rich men... they are incapable of carrying on any war... fondness for money makes them unwilling to pay taxes... such a State will have both the extremes of great wealth and utter poverty... whenever you see paupers in a State, somewhere in that neighborhood there are hidden away thieves, and cut-purses and robbers...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify oligarchy by property qualifications, social division, neglect of virtue, criminality bred by poverty, and practical weaknesses (e.g., inability to wage war or govern effectively).
